paragraphs.text: Wherefore thou art without excuse, O man, whosoever thou art that judgest: for wherein thou judges another, thou condemnest thyself; for thou that judgest dost practise the same things.
paragraphs.original: Διὸ ἀναπολόγητος εἶ, ὦ ἄνθρωπε πᾶς ὁ κρίνων· ἐν ᾧ γὰρ κρίνεις τὸν ἕτερον, σεαυτὸν κατακρίνεις, τὰ γὰρ αὐτὰ πράσσεις ὁ κρίνων·
paragraphs.translit: Dio anapologētos ei, ō anthrōpe pas ho krinōn· en hō gar krineis ton heteron, seauton katakrineis, ta gar auta prasseis ho krinōn·

paragraphs.text: And we know that the judgment of God is according to truth against them that practise such things.
paragraphs.original: οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι τὸ κρίμα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν κατὰ ἀλήθειαν ἐπὶ τοὺς τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντας.
paragraphs.translit: oidamen de hoti to krima tou theou estin kata alētheian epi tous ta toiauta prassontas.

paragraphs.text: And reckonest thou this, O man, who judgest them that practise such things, and doest the same, that thou shalt escape the judgment of God?
paragraphs.original: λογίζῃ δὲ τοῦτο, ὦ ἄνθρωπε ὁ κρίνων τοὺς τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντας καὶ ποιῶν αὐτά, ὅτι σὺ ἐκφεύξῃ τὸ κρίμα τοῦ θεοῦ;
paragraphs.translit: logizē de touto, ō anthrōpe ho krinōn tous ta toiauta prassontas kai poiōn auta, hoti sy ekpheuxē to krima tou theou;

paragraphs.text: Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering, not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance?
paragraphs.original: ἢ τοῦ πλούτου τῆς χρηστότητος αὐτοῦ καὶ τῆς ἀνοχῆς καὶ τῆς μακροθυμίας καταφρονεῖς, ἀγνοῶν ὅτι τὸ χρηστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς μετάνοιάν σε ἄγει;
paragraphs.translit: ē tou ploutou tēs chrēstotētos autou kai tēs anochēs kai tēs makrothymias kataphroneis, agnoōn hoti to chrēston tou theou eis metanoian se agei;

paragraphs.text: but after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up for thyself wrath in the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God;
paragraphs.original: κατὰ δὲ τὴν σκληρότητά σου καὶ ἀμετανόητον καρδίαν θησαυρίζεις σεαυτῷ ὀργὴν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ὀργῆς καὶ ἀποκαλύψεως δικαιοκρισίας τοῦ θεοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: kata de tēn sklērotēta sou kai ametanoēton kardian thēsaurizeis seautō orgēn en hēmera orgēs kai apokalypseōs dikaiokrisias tou theou,

paragraphs.text: who will render to every man according to his works:
paragraphs.original: ὃς ἀποδώσει ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: hos apodōsei hekastō kata ta erga autou·

paragraphs.text: to them that by patience in well-doing seek for glory and honor and incorruption, eternal life:
paragraphs.original: τοῖς μὲν καθʼ ὑπομονὴν ἔργου ἀγαθοῦ δόξαν καὶ τιμὴν καὶ ἀφθαρσίαν ζητοῦσιν ζωὴν αἰώνιον·
paragraphs.translit: tois men kathʼ hypomonēn ergou agathou doxan kai timēn kai aphtharsian zētousin zōēn aiōnion·

paragraphs.text: but unto them that are factious, and obey not the truth, but obey unrighteousness, [shall be] wrath and indignation,
paragraphs.original: τοῖς δὲ ἐξ ἐριθείας καὶ ἀπειθοῦσι τῇ ἀληθείᾳ πειθομένοις δὲ τῇ ἀδικίᾳ ὀργὴ καὶ θυμός,
paragraphs.translit: tois de ex eritheias kai apeithousi tē alētheia peithomenois de tē adikia orgē kai thymos,

paragraphs.text: tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that worketh evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Greek;
paragraphs.original: θλῖψις καὶ στενοχωρία, ἐπὶ πᾶσαν ψυχὴν ἀνθρώπου τοῦ κατεργαζομένου τὸ κακόν, Ἰουδαίου τε πρῶτον καὶ Ἕλληνος·
paragraphs.translit: thlipsis kai stenochōria, epi pasan psychēn anthrōpou tou katergazomenou to kakon, Ioudaiou te prōton kai Hellēnos·

paragraphs.text: but glory and honor and peace to every man that worketh good, to the Jew first, and also to the Greek:
paragraphs.original: δόξα δὲ καὶ τιμὴ καὶ εἰρήνη παντὶ τῷ ἐργαζομένῳ τὸ ἀγαθόν, Ἰουδαίῳ τε πρῶτον καὶ Ἕλληνι·
paragraphs.translit: doxa de kai timē kai eirēnē panti tō ergazomenō to agathon, Ioudaiō te prōton kai Hellēni·

paragraphs.text: for there is no respect of persons with God.
paragraphs.original: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν προσωπολημψία παρὰ τῷ θεῷ.
paragraphs.translit: ou gar estin prosōpolēmpsia para tō theō.

paragraphs.text: For as many as have sinned without law shall also perish without the law: and as many as have sinned under the law shall be judged by the law;
paragraphs.original: Ὅσοι γὰρ ἀνόμως ἥμαρτον, ἀνόμως καὶ ἀπολοῦνται· καὶ ὅσοι ἐν νόμῳ ἥμαρτον, διὰ νόμου κριθήσονται·
paragraphs.translit: Hosoi gar anomōs hēmarton, anomōs kai apolountai· kai hosoi en nomō hēmarton, dia nomou krithēsontai·

paragraphs.text: for not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified:
paragraphs.original: οὐ γὰρ οἱ ἀκροαταὶ νόμου δίκαιοι παρὰ τῷ θεῷ, ἀλλʼ οἱ ποιηταὶ νόμου δικαιωθήσονται.
paragraphs.translit: ou gar hoi akroatai nomou dikaioi para tō theō, allʼ hoi poiētai nomou dikaiōthēsontai.

paragraphs.text: (for when Gentiles that have not the law do by nature the things of the law, these, not having the law, are the law unto themselves;
paragraphs.original: ὅταν γὰρ ἔθνη τὰ μὴ νόμον ἔχοντα φύσει τὰ τοῦ νόμου ποιῶσιν, οὗτοι νόμον μὴ ἔχοντες ἑαυτοῖς εἰσιν νόμος·
paragraphs.translit: hotan gar ethnē ta mē nomon echonta physei ta tou nomou poiōsin, houtoi nomon mē echontes heautois eisin nomos·

paragraphs.text: in that they show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience bearing witness therewith, and their thoughts one with another accusing or else excusing [them]);
paragraphs.original: οἵτινες ἐνδείκνυνται τὸ ἔργον τοῦ νόμου γραπτὸν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν, συμμαρτυρούσης αὐτῶν τῆς συνειδήσεως καὶ μεταξὺ ἀλλήλων τῶν λογισμῶν κατηγορούντων ἢ καὶ ἀπολογουμένων,
paragraphs.translit: hoitines endeiknyntai to ergon tou nomou grapton en tais kardiais autōn, symmartyrousēs autōn tēs syneidēseōs kai metaxy allēlōn tōn logismōn katēgorountōn ē kai apologoumenōn,

paragraphs.text: in the day when God shall judge the secrets of men, according to my gospel, by Jesus Christ.
paragraphs.original: ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ὅτε κρίνει ὁ θεὸς τὰ κρυπτὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιόν μου διὰ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: en hēmera hote krinei ho theos ta krypta tōn anthrōpōn kata to euangelion mou dia Christou Iēsou.

paragraphs.text: But if thou bearest the name of a Jew, and restest upon the law, and gloriest in God,
paragraphs.original: Εἰ δὲ σὺ Ἰουδαῖος ἐπονομάζῃ καὶ ἐπαναπαύῃ νόμῳ καὶ καυχᾶσαι ἐν θεῷ
paragraphs.translit: Ei de sy Ioudaios eponomazē kai epanapauē nomō kai kauchasai en theō

paragraphs.text: and knowest his will, and approvest the things that are excellent, being instructed out of the law,
paragraphs.original: καὶ γινώσκεις τὸ θέλημα καὶ δοκιμάζεις τὰ διαφέροντα κατηχούμενος ἐκ τοῦ νόμου,
paragraphs.translit: kai ginōskeis to thelēma kai dokimazeis ta diapheronta katēchoumenos ek tou nomou,

paragraphs.text: and art confident that thou thyself art a guide of the blind, a light of them that are in darkness,
paragraphs.original: πέποιθάς τε σεαυτὸν ὁδηγὸν εἶναι τυφλῶν, φῶς τῶν ἐν σκότει,
paragraphs.translit: pepoithas te seauton hodēgon einai typhlōn, phōs tōn en skotei,

paragraphs.text: a corrector of the foolish, a teacher of babes, having in the law the form of knowledge and of the truth;
paragraphs.original: παιδευτὴν ἀφρόνων, διδάσκαλον νηπίων, ἔχοντα τὴν μόρφωσιν τῆς γνώσεως καὶ τῆς ἀληθείας ἐν τῷ νόμῳ—
paragraphs.translit: paideutēn aphronōn, didaskalon nēpiōn, echonta tēn morphōsin tēs gnōseōs kai tēs alētheias en tō nomō—

paragraphs.text: thou therefore that teachest another, teachest thou not thyself? thou that preachest a man should not steal, dost thou steal?
paragraphs.original: ὁ οὖν διδάσκων ἕτερον σεαυτὸν οὐ διδάσκεις; ὁ κηρύσσων μὴ κλέπτειν κλέπτεις;
paragraphs.translit: ho oun didaskōn heteron seauton ou didaskeis; ho kēryssōn mē kleptein klepteis;

paragraphs.text: thou that sayest a man should not commit adultery, dost thou commit adultery? thou that abhorrest idols, dost thou rob temples?
paragraphs.original: ὁ λέγων μὴ μοιχεύειν μοιχεύεις; ὁ βδελυσσόμενος τὰ εἴδωλα ἱεροσυλεῖς;
paragraphs.translit: ho legōn mē moicheuein moicheueis; ho bdelyssomenos ta eidōla hierosyleis;

paragraphs.text: thou who gloriest in the law, through thy transgression of the law dishonorest thou God?
paragraphs.original: ὃς ἐν νόμῳ καυχᾶσαι, διὰ τῆς παραβάσεως τοῦ νόμου τὸν θεὸν ἀτιμάζεις;
paragraphs.translit: hos en nomō kauchasai, dia tēs parabaseōs tou nomou ton theon atimazeis;

paragraphs.text: For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you, even as it is written.
paragraphs.original: τὸ γὰρ ὄνομα τοῦ θεοῦ διʼ ὑμᾶς βλασφημεῖται ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, καθὼς γέγραπται.
paragraphs.translit: to gar onoma tou theou diʼ hymas blasphēmeitai en tois ethnesin, kathōs gegraptai.

paragraphs.text: For circumcision indeed profiteth, if thou be a doer of the law: but if thou be a transgressor of the law, thy circumcision is become uncircumcision.
paragraphs.original: Περιτομὴ μὲν γὰρ ὠφελεῖ ἐὰν νόμον πράσσῃς· ἐὰν δὲ παραβάτης νόμου ᾖς, ἡ περιτομή σου ἀκροβυστία γέγονεν.
paragraphs.translit: Peritomē men gar ōphelei ean nomon prassēs· ean de parabatēs nomou ēs, hē peritomē sou akrobystia gegonen.

paragraphs.text: If therefore the uncircumcision keep the ordinances of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be reckoned for circumcision?
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν οὖν ἡ ἀκροβυστία τὰ δικαιώματα τοῦ νόμου φυλάσσῃ, οὐχ ἡ ἀκροβυστία αὐτοῦ εἰς περιτομὴν λογισθήσεται;
paragraphs.translit: ean oun hē akrobystia ta dikaiōmata tou nomou phylassē, ouch hē akrobystia autou eis peritomēn logisthēsetai;

paragraphs.text: and shall not the uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfil the law, judge thee, who with the letter and circumcision art a transgressor of the law?
paragraphs.original: καὶ κρινεῖ ἡ ἐκ φύσεως ἀκροβυστία τὸν νόμον τελοῦσα σὲ τὸν διὰ γράμματος καὶ περιτομῆς παραβάτην νόμου.
paragraphs.translit: kai krinei hē ek physeōs akrobystia ton nomon telousa se ton dia grammatos kai peritomēs parabatēn nomou.

paragraphs.text: For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision which is outward in the flesh:
paragraphs.original: οὐ γὰρ ὁ ἐν τῷ φανερῷ Ἰουδαῖός ἐστιν, οὐδὲ ἡ ἐν τῷ φανερῷ ἐν σαρκὶ περιτομή·
paragraphs.translit: ou gar ho en tō phanerō Ioudaios estin, oude hē en tō phanerō en sarki peritomē·

paragraphs.text: but he is a Jew who is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλʼ ὁ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ Ἰουδαῖος, καὶ περιτομὴ καρδίας ἐν πνεύματι οὐ γράμματι, οὗ ὁ ἔπαινος οὐκ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἀλλʼ ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: allʼ ho en tō kryptō Ioudaios, kai peritomē kardias en pneumati ou grammati, hou ho epainos ouk ex anthrōpōn allʼ ek tou theou.
